item.title: Chinese crystal breaks record in race to build nuclear clocks
item.description:
Scientists in China have created the world's first crystal capable of producing the ultraviolet light needed to power thorium nuclear clocks, a development that could one day enable submarines and deep-space probes to navigate without GPS.

The fluorinated borate compound, developed by a team led by Pan Shilie at the Xinjiang Technical Institute of Physics and Chemistry, can push laser light down to a record 145.2 nanometres — short enough to meet a critical requirement for these ultra-precise, compact timekeepers, the South China Morning Post reported. The research was published in the journal Advanced Materials earlier this year.

item.title: IRGC claims full control of Strait of Hormuz after Trump orders blockade
item.description:
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps declared on Sunday that its naval forces have assumed full control over all maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, issuing a sharp warning to Washington just hours after President Trump announced a U.S. naval blockade of the critical waterway.

In a statement posted in Persian on X, accompanied by video footage appearing to show vessels targeted in crosshairs, the IRGC naval command said "all traffic is under the full control of the armed forces" and warned that "the enemy will become trapped in a deadly vortex in the Strait if it makes the wrong move". The declaration came as a direct response to Trump's announcement on Truth Social that the U.S. Navy would "effective immediately" begin blockading all ships attempting to enter or leave the strait.

item.title: Russia, Ukraine trade thousands of violation claims as Easter ceasefire crumbles
item.description: A 32-hour Orthodox Easter ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine fell apart within hours of taking effect, with both sides accusing each other of thousands of breaches by Sunday morning. The truce, declared by Russian President Vladimir Putin on April 9 and effective from 4 p.m. on Saturday, was intended to cover the Easter holiday through the end of Sunday.

item.title: IRGC warns military vessels near Hormuz will breach ceasefire
item.description: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps declared on Sunday that any military vessel approaching the Strait of Hormuz would be considered a violation of the fragile US-Iran ceasefire and would be met with a "firm and forceful response," escalating a standoff over the world's most critical oil chokepoint as peace talks collapsed without an agreement.

item.title: Orban concedes as Magyar's Tisza wins Hungary election
item.description:
Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orban conceded defeat on Sunday night to opposition leader Peter Magyar, whose Tisza party was on course to win a commanding majority in the country's parliamentary election, ending 16 years of uninterrupted rule by Orban's Fidesz party.

Magyar announced the victory in a social media post, saying that Orban had personally sent his congratulations on the election win, according to Euronews. Reuters reported that Orban conceded after projections showed Tisza winning a two-thirds supermajority in the 199-seat National Assembly.

item.title: UK refuses to join Trump's Strait of Hormuz blockade
item.description:
The United Kingdom confirmed on Sunday that it will not join President Donald Trump's newly announced naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, directly contradicting Trump's own claims that Britain was among the countries assisting with the operation.

Trump announced the blockade in a post on Truth Social hours after US-Iran peace talks in Islamabad collapsed without a deal. "Effective immediately, the United States Navy, the Finest in the World, will begin the process of BLOCKADING any and all Ships trying to enter, or leave, the Strait of Hormuz," he wrote. In a later interview with Fox News, Trump said, "The U.K. and a couple of other countries are sending mine sweepers".

That claim was swiftly rebuffed by London. A UK government spokesperson told CBS News that Britain would not be involved in the blockade and was instead "urgently working with France and other partners to put together a wide coalition to protect freedom of navigation". The spokesperson added: "The Strait of Hormuz must not be subject to tolling".

item.title: U.S.-Iran talks end without deal as UN chief calls Hormuz tolls unlawful
item.description: The head of the International Maritime Organization declared that Iran's effort to levy tolls on vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz is unlawful and must be resisted by the international community, as shipping through the critical waterway remains a fraction of pre-war levels despite a fragile ceasefire now days old.

item.title: An Iraqi drone narrowly missed a convoy carrying a freed US journalist in Baghdad
item.description: A drone attack by an unidentified Iran-backed Iraqi militia narrowly missed a U.S. diplomatic convoy transporting freed American journalist Shelly Kittleson through Baghdad International Airport on April 8, according to a senior Iraqi security official who spoke to Agence France-Presse. The incident, which came just one day after Kittleson's release from a week of captivity, underscored the persistent dangers facing American personnel in Iraq amid escalating regional hostilities.

item.title: CENTCOM to begin blockade of Iranian ports Monday
item.description: U.S. Central Command announced Sunday that American naval forces will begin enforcing a blockade of all maritime traffic entering and exiting Iranian ports on Monday, April 13, at 10 a.m. ET, following President Donald Trump's order after U.S.-Iran nuclear negotiations ended without an agreement. The blockade marks a dramatic escalation in the conflict that has upended global energy markets since late February.

item.title: McIlroy wins back-to-back Masters titles at Augusta
item.description: Rory McIlroy claimed his second consecutive green jacket on Sunday at Augusta National, finishing at 12 under par to become the fourth player in Masters history to win the tournament in back-to-back years, joining Jack Nicklaus, Nick Faldo, and Tiger Woods.

item.title: Israeli strike kills toddler at her father's funeral in southern Lebanon
item.description:
Israeli military strikes killed at least 97 people and wounded 133 others across southern Lebanon in a single 24-hour period ending Saturday, pushing the cumulative death toll past 2,000 since the war between Israel and Hezbollah erupted on March 2, according to Lebanon's Health Ministry.

The ministry said in a statement Saturday evening that at least 2,020 people have now been killed and 6,436 wounded, including 165 children and 248 women. Nearly one million people have been displaced from their homes across the country.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV calls for ceasefire in Ukraine, Lebanon, Sudan
item.description:
Pope Leo XIV issued urgent appeals for peace in Ukraine, Lebanon, and Sudan on Sunday, using his Regina Caeli address on Divine Mercy Sunday to call on warring parties to lay down their arms and protect civilians caught in conflict.

Speaking to pilgrims gathered in St. Peter's Square on April 12, the pope invoked international humanitarian principles as he demanded immediate action. "The principle of humanity, inscribed in the conscience of every person and recognized in international law, entails the moral obligation to protect the civilian population from the horrific effects of war," he said. "I call on the parties in the conflict to declare a ceasefire and urgently seek a peaceful solution."

item.title: Starmer and Macron agree on Hormuz coalition in call after Iran talks collapse
item.description:
UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer and French President Emmanuel Macron spoke by phone on Sunday, agreeing on the need for de-escalation across the Middle East and pledging joint efforts to protect freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, according to an official readout from Downing Street .

The leaders stressed the importance of a lasting ceasefire that includes Lebanon to support wider regional stability, and agreed on the "strategic importance of the Strait of Hormuz for global trade and energy supplies," the readout said, adding that both would work "with a wide coalition of partners to protect freedom of navigation" .

item.title: Iran's internet blackout hits 44 days as US talks collapse
item.description: Iran's nationwide internet blackout has entered its 44th consecutive day, surpassing 1,032 hours and setting what monitors describe as the longest nation-scale internet shutdown ever recorded in any country. The milestone comes as high-stakes peace talks between Washington and Tehran collapsed in Islamabad on Sunday without agreement, casting doubt over a fragile ceasefire set to expire on 22 April.

item.title: Trump calls Pope Leo XIV 'weak' as Vatican feud escalates over Iran war
item.description:
President Donald Trump launched a broadside against Pope Leo XIV on Sunday, calling the pontiff "WEAK on Crime, and terrible for Foreign Policy" in a social media post that marked the sharpest public clash yet between the White House and the Vatican over the U.S.-led war in Iran.

Writing on Truth Social, Trump urged the first American-born pope to "stop appeasing the Radical Left," escalating a weeks-long feud that has pitted the world's two most prominent Americans against each other on opposite sides of the conflict.

item.title: Starmer and Macron call for de-escalation and Lebanon ceasefire
item.description: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer and French President Emmanuel Macron spoke on Sunday, April 12, issuing a joint call for de-escalation in the Middle East and insisting that any ceasefire must extend to Lebanon, according to an official readout from Downing Street. The conversation came hours after US President Donald Trump announced the US Navy would blockade the Strait of Hormuz following the collapse of marathon peace talks between the US and Iran in Islamabad.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV arrives in Algeria on historic first papal visit
item.description: Pope Leo XIV departed Rome on Monday for Algeria, becoming the first pope ever to visit the North African nation and launching an ambitious 11-day tour of four African countries aimed at strengthening Christian-Muslim dialogue and honoring the legacy of St. Augustine.

item.title: South Korea, Poland upgrade ties in first shift in 13 years
item.description:
South Korean President Lee Jae-myung and Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk agreed on Monday to elevate bilateral relations to a "comprehensive strategic partnership," marking the first upgrade in ties since the two countries established a strategic partnership in 2013.

The announcement came during a summit at Cheong Wa Dae in Seoul, during what was the first bilateral visit by a Polish prime minister to South Korea in 27 years and Tusk's first bilateral visit to a non-European country since taking office.

item.title: Wise reports 26% Q4 volume surge ahead of May Nasdaq debut
item.description:
British fintech group Wise reported on Monday that cross-border transaction volumes rose 26 percent in the fourth quarter to £49.4 billion ($66.2 billion), reinforcing expectations that its full-year profit margin will land at the top end of its forecast range as the company prepares for its Nasdaq debut.

The London-listed money transfer firm said it expects to complete its planned dual listing and begin trading on the Nasdaq from May 11, marking a milestone in its shift toward the US capital markets. As part of the transition, Wise will report its fiscal 2026 results in US dollars under US GAAP accounting standards.

item.title: China's Q1 GDP expected to rebound to 4.8% amid Iran war risks
item.description:
China's economy is expected to have regained momentum in the first quarter of 2026, but economists warn that the ongoing war in Iran threatens to drag on growth for the rest of the year as energy costs rise and global demand weakens.

Gross domestic product likely grew 4.8% year-on-year in the January-March period, up from a 4.5% pace in the fourth quarter of 2025, according to a Reuters poll of 50 economists published on Monday. The rebound was driven by robust exports, particularly in electronics and AI-related products, and recovering investment. Beijing is scheduled to release the official Q1 GDP figures alongside March activity data on Thursday, April 16.
